narration.full_text: Now, let's put our knowledge of HCF and LCM to the test with some real-world word problems. These types of problems often appear in exams, so understanding how to approach them is crucial. We'll learn to identify whether a problem requires finding the Highest Common Factor or the Least Common Multiple. This distinction is key to solving them correctly. For example, if you're trying to divide things into equal groups or find the largest possible measure, you'll likely use HCF. On the other hand, if you're looking for when events will next coincide or the smallest common quantity, LCM is your tool. We'll walk through a few examples together, breaking down each step to ensure you grasp the underlying logic. Pay close attention to the wording of each problem, as it often contains clues about which method to apply. By the end of this section, you'll feel confident tackling these problems on your own.
